items.title: Vellum reverses course on AI automation after author backlash
items.excerpt: Mac book-formatting app Vellum pulled its new 'Automation' feature, which let authors connect external AI assistants to manage back-catalogue tasks, in version 4.2.1 just days after launch following a wave of criticism from indie authors (Vellum blog: 'We've Removed Vellum Automation', Nov 5).

items.title: RNIB poll: 65% won't listen to AI audiobooks
items.excerpt: A YouGov poll for the RNIB, marking 90 years of its Talking Books service, finds 65% of UK adults won't listen to AI-narrated audiobooks and shows what makes listeners abandon a narrator's voice.

history_match.title: YouTube looks to expand into audiobooks

items.title: Drama scripts and webtoons, too, are being created with AI
items.excerpt: Korean creators are learning to develop characters, plots and webtoon storyboards step by step with generative AI in hands-on courses, as AI-assisted story creation spreads from scripts to webtoons.

history_match.title: [Korean Startup Interview] Sodalive: Turning Finished Webtoon Characters into AI Creators

items.title: AI로 하루 10권 '딸깍 출판'...커지는 전자책 시장 명암
items.excerpt: 생성형 AI로 개인이 하루에도 여러 권의 전자책을 찍어내는 '딸깍 출판'이 확산되지만, AI 활용 고지 기준과 품질 검증 장치가 없어 전자책 소비자 불만도 함께 늘고 있다.

items.title: The 2026 PW Salary & Jobs Report: 73% of publishers use AI, 77% of staff view it negatively
items.excerpt: PW's survey of 886 publishing workers finds 73% say their company uses AI (market research leads), yet 77% hold a negative view of the technology; the top worry is ending up publishing a book substantially written by AI.

items.title: SIBF 2026: Booker-winning translator Daisy Rockwell on whether AI threatens writing
items.excerpt: International Booker winner Daisy Rockwell, translator of Tomb of Sand, says at the Sharjah International Book Fair that while AI has entered literature, its role in literary translation and creative writing remains limited.

items.title: Sharjah Translation Award debate highlights limits of AI in literary translation
items.excerpt: Translators, academics and publishers at the Sharjah Translation Award seminar at SIBF 2026 said AI can speed up translation but cannot replace human judgment on cultural nuance and literary voice.

history_match.title: AI platform wins publishing award in Sharjah

items.title: Steins;Gate developer MAGES says AI translation is a long way from viable for visual novels
items.excerpt: MAGES president Makoto Asada says machine translation can't yet handle the text-heavy, nuance-dependent writing of visual novels, explaining the studio's stance on AI localization.

items.title: What AI can't learn about peer review, because nobody can explain it
items.excerpt: A guest post argues that publishers automating peer review with AI risk losing tacit editorial expertise that has never been made explicit enough to train or evaluate a model on.

items.title: Literary prizes are for writers, not machines
items.excerpt: As publishers cut ties with authors accused of using AI, Prospect argues France's new prize for AI-co-written manuscripts sends the wrong message, amid the Goncourt AI-use row.

history_match.title: New literary prize Prix Pascal launches in France for manuscripts written with AI

items.title: AI's role in book publishing raises questions about quality, transparency
items.excerpt: Gray Media report on how AI is changing how authors write, edit and publish books, and readers' growing questions about quality and disclosure of AI-assisted titles.

items.title: From AI adoption to AI practice: building governed AI in scholarly publishing
items.excerpt: How a publisher can make AI useful across the organization while keeping control of confidential manuscripts, editorial decisions and accountability: a practical governance framework.

history_match.title: Guest Post – Artificial Intelligence in Scholarly Publishing: Are We Moving Faster Than the Evidence?

items.title: OpenAI copyright suit draws more than 50 amicus briefs
items.excerpt: More than 50 amicus briefs filed in the authors' and publishers' copyright case against OpenAI map the fault lines of the most closely watched AI training lawsuit and what's at stake for books.

history_match.title: Publishers urge US court to reject OpenAI's fair use defence in copyright case

items.title: Litigation, but growing use of AI in book publishing
items.excerpt: Big Five publishers are suing AI companies even as AI use grows inside their houses, from internal assistants to marketing tools, illustrating the industry's crosscurrents.

history_match.title: Macmillan Staff Say the Publisher Threw a Party for a Workplace AI Assistant That Was Later Killed

items.title: Why the AI detection scandals will end, probably quite soon
items.excerpt: Jane Friedman argues 2026's AI-use allegations against authors stem from books acquired before publishers adopted detection tools like Pangram, so the scandals should fade as screening moves upstream.

items.title: "사람이 쓴 소설만 읽고 싶어"…웹소설계 번지는 'AI 염증'
items.excerpt: 생성형 AI로 웹소설 원고가 대량 생산되면서 독자들 사이에서 'AI 염증'이 번지고, 플랫폼과 작가들이 AI 작품 표기와 검수 문제로 고민하고 있다.
